title: Epic: KMS integration hardening + rotation docs (Security & Compliance Foundation)
creator: Naomi Feldman
project: Security & Compliance Foundation — KMS integration hardening + rotation docs
description:
Overview
We are expanding Private and Dedicated deployments for regulated customers. This epic hardens Redwood’s KMS/HSM-backed envelope encryption integrations (control-plane + data-plane) and publishes a rotation procedure that is repeatable, auditable, and resilient under KMS failure modes.

Primary outcomes
1) Integration hardening
- Standardize KMS client wrapper across call sites (timeouts, retry budgets, jitter/backoff, circuit breaking, and safe defaults).
- Canonical error taxonomy that is consistent in logs, metrics, and customer-facing errors.
- Guardrails to prevent unsafe prod configs (e.g., retry amplification, infinite retry, excessively long timeouts).

2) Rotation workflow + evidence
- Define KEK/DEK key versioning strategy (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private notes), including staged rollout, verification, and rollback.
- Produce evidence-friendly artifacts for audits: checklist + rotation log template + required approvals.
- Add explicit audit-log events for rotation-related config changes (cutover toggles, key version updates).

3) Failure-mode testing + readiness
- CI/staging integration tests covering throttling/timeouts, AccessDenied, key disabled/NotFound, and ciphertext mismatch.
- Game day for KMS degradation/outage; publish after-action with follow-ups.
- Operator runbooks and Private deployment operator guide updates (preflight validation, troubleshooting matrix).

Scope (in)
- KMS client wrapper library in monorepo used by: control plane services, data plane components that decrypt configuration/secrets, installer preflight validation paths.
- Telemetry requirements: latency histograms, error counters by canonical category, tracing spans with consistent tags, health check endpoint.
- Rotation procedure and documentation updates (internal runbooks + customer-facing operator guide).

Scope (out)
- Net-new cryptographic algorithms or major crypto primitive changes.
- Broad auth revamp unrelated to KMS key management.

Key dependencies / linked artifacts
- Confluence ADRs: ADR-007 (KMS wrapper + failure policy), ADR-008 (rotation dual-read/cutover)
- Implementation PRs (expected):
  - Monorepo: kms client abstraction, metrics + tracing, circuit breaker, caching semantics, dual-read support, guardrails, healthcheck endpoint, audit log events
  - Private installer: preflight validation + permission checks
  - Terraform: least-privilege KMS IAM modules; separation of runtime decrypt vs rotation roles
  - Docs: Private operator guide; rotation procedure + evidence checklist

Rollout plan (staged)
- Phase 0: Wrapper shipped behind feature flags; metrics and trace spans validated in staging.
- Phase 1: Canary (one internal region + low-traffic Dedicated tenant), with tight rollback triggers.
- Phase 2: Expand to all Hosted regions; enable per-service.
- Phase 3: Private deployments: new installer preflight + operator guide; backport for existing Private customers as optional upgrade.

Proposed rollback / safety criteria
- Rollback if KMS-related 5xx increases >0.25% absolute over baseline for 15m in any prod region, or if p95 decrypt latency increases >50ms sustained.
- Rollback if evidence/audit events are missing for key-version changes in staging rehearsal.
- For rotation dual-read: rollback if decrypt mismatch errors appear >0.01% or if any ciphertext cannot be decrypted by both expected key versions during verification window.

Success metrics
- Reliability: reduce KMS-induced elevated error incidents; eliminate retry amplification patterns under timeout spikes.
- Observability: 100% of KMS calls emit standardized metrics + trace spans with canonical error categories.
- Operability: preflight validation catches the top 3 Private customer misconfigs (wrong ARN/key ID, missing kms:Decrypt, wrong principal/role).
- Compliance: rotation evidence template used in at least 2 enterprise security reviews without bespoke follow-up questions.

Notes / risks
- Risk: overly aggressive retries can amplify KMS load (observed near-miss); wrapper must enforce retry budgets + jitter + circuit break.
- Risk: rotation cutover complexity in mixed-version deployments; dual-read flags must be designed to avoid partial cutover states.
- Risk: customer-managed KMS policies vary widely; docs must include actionable errors and a clear troubleshooting matrix.

Comms
- Weekly sync: #eng-security + #eng-platform, with SRE check-in before enabling in prod.
- Release checkpoints: Connor O’Brien owns go/no-go and sign-off doc; Security and SRE must approve before Phase 2.
